facts.statement: IPO eligibility on IFSC exchanges (any one test): operating revenue of at least USD 20 million (last FY or 3-year average), OR pre-tax profit of at least USD 1 million, OR post-issue market cap of at least USD 25 million, OR startup/SME route.

Listing process: offer-document filing for IFSCA observations is exempt when issue size is USD 100 million or less; the offer must be made within 18 months of the observation letter; financial information must not be older than 135 days; IFRS, US GAAP or Ind AS are accepted (home-jurisdiction standards require IFRS reconciliation); the offer period is a minimum of 1 and maximum of 10 working days.
facts.detail: IFSCA (Listing) (Amendment) Regulations, 2025 extended the financial-information timeline to 180 days and cut allotment/refund to 8 working days with half-yearly post-listing disclosure (13 October 2025).

facts.statement: Minimum public offer: Indian/IFSC companies follow SCRR norms; foreign companies must offer at least 10% of post-issue paid-up capital and maintain it continuously. Promoter/controlling-shareholder lock-up is 180 days from allotment.

IFSC SPAC framework: the acquisition target is not identified before the IPO; sponsors hold 15-20% of post-issue capital; offer size is at least USD 50 million; minimum application is USD 100,000; the acquisition must complete within 3 years; escrow plus redemption/liquidation provisions are mandatory.

Depository Receipts: minimum offer/subscription USD 700,000 with allotment, payments and refunds within 5 working days. Commercial Paper listing: maturity 7 days to 1 year, issued at discount, no call/put options, no underwriting, demat form, listing fee USD 1,000; Certificate of Deposit: demat form, listing fee USD 1,000.

Credit rating by an IFSCA-registered CRA became mandatory for listed debt securities from 1 October 2024; ESG-labelled debt covers green, social and sustainability-linked bonds under recognised international frameworks.

The Transition Bond Framework was issued on 29 July 2025 targeting hard-to-abate sectors (steel, cement, chemicals, aviation, shipping) with four pillars: credible transition plans, taxonomic alignment, independent external review, and comprehensive disclosure; opportunity sizing is USD 251 billion (steel) and USD 141 billion (cement) by 2030, referencing EU/Japan/Singapore/ASEAN/Australian taxonomies and integrating with GEI Target Rules 2025 and CCTS.
facts.detail: Transition Bonds and ISSB S2 covered in ICSI CSJ January 2026.

facts.statement: LEAP Rules 2024 (Companies (Listing of Equity Shares in Permissible Jurisdictions) Rules 2024, with FEMA NDI Amendment Rules 2024) enable Indian public companies to list equity shares directly on IFSC exchanges; shares are demat and pari passu with domestic shares, with the prospectus filed via e-Form LEAP-1 within 7 days.

RBI's scheme for Sovereign Gold Bond trading/settlement in IFSC came in August 2024 with IFSCA operating guidelines in September 2024; FPI holding in SGrBs is only 2.228%, the FAR route is used, and fungibility exists between the IFSC and RBI ecosystems.

IFSC debt market FY2024-25: 57 issuances raising USD 6.99 billion, 100% USD-denominated; NBFCs accounted for 50 of 57 issuances (USD 5.23 billion); fixed-rate 22 issuances (USD 6.66 billion, 95% of value, coupons 3.75-9.7% averaging 6.63%); floating 35 issuances (SOFR spreads +0.95% to +5.0%, average +4.43%); all private placements; ESG bonds 39.4% of total.
facts.detail: Top issuers: Muthoot USD 650M, Continuum Trinethra Renewables USD 650M, SBI USD 500M, REC USD 500M, Shriram Finance USD 500M (~40% combined). Exchange split: India INX 76% (44 listings) vs NSE IFSC 24% (14).

facts.statement: IFSCA (Capital Market Intermediaries) Regulations, 2025 (notified 17 April 2025) replaced the 2021 regulations and cover: broker-dealers, clearing members, custodians, depository participants, investment bankers, investment advisers, distributors, credit rating agencies, ESG Ratings and Data Products Providers (ERDPP), and research entities.
facts.detail: Obligations include record-keeping, risk management, cyber and cyber-resilience, grievance redressal, business continuity, annual compliance audit, fit-and-proper, and mandatory Principal Officer + Compliance Officer. Master Circulars for 7 CMI categories were issued 5 August 2025.

facts.statement: The CMI revised Principal Officer/Compliance Officer norms deadline was extended twice - to 31 December 2025 (4 September 2025 circular) and then to 15 January 2026 (amendments notified 12 January 2026) or publication of the CMI Amendment Regulations 2026, whichever earlier; a certification course for CMI KMPs and employees was specified in April 2026.
facts.detail: Liquid net worth clarifications under CMI Regs 2025 were issued 30 December 2025.

facts.statement: Capital market trajectory: exchange turnover USD 219 billion (FY22) → USD 447 billion (FY23, +104%) → USD 711 billion (FY24, +59%) → USD 1,125 billion (FY25, +58.2%); demat accounts 65,227 (Mar-25) rising to 69,280 (Dec-25); cumulative debt listed USD 65.10 billion with ESG-labelled USD 15.43 billion (FY25), rising to USD 68.03 billion / USD 16.19 billion ESG by Dec-2025.
facts.detail: GIFT NIFTY average monthly turnover USD 93 billion; GIFT SENSEX launched on India INX; aggregate open interest USD 12 billion (FY25).

facts.statement: India's equity market capitalisation crossed USD 5 trillion; the Standing Committee on Primary Markets is chaired by Mohandas Pai; the framework benchmarks IOSCO Principles 16-18.
